summary.text: A 46-year-old man had a cochlear implant placed in the right ear in 2013 because of profound binaural sensorineural hearing loss. Five years after the implant he presented with otorrhoea of 8 months duration in the implanted ear. The implant had been functioning normally, but otoscopic examination revealed an electrode array protruding through the external auditory canal.

Endoscope-assisted revision surgery via the posterior external auditory canal covered the exposed electrode and repaired the broken posterior canal wall. A tragal cartilage-perichondrium graft was harvested, ear wax, pus and scabs were removed, the field was disinfected, the electrode array was confirmed well positioned within the cochlea, rotated and pushed back into the mastoid cavity, and the graft was inserted through the perforation before the meatus was packed.
The performance of the right implant was the same as before the revision surgery. Outpatient follow-up 12 months after surgery confirmed the integrity of the external auditory canal repair.
